verdict.summary: OAuth exists only for approved App Shop partners: you apply to the technology partner program, build in a sandbox, and the install must start and end inside Rippling's App Shop flow, with SSO, user management and an Integration Review before outside companies can install. Customers also need Rippling's Identity & Access Management package, and private scopes (the richer employee data) are 'extremely limited'.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Sandbox, partner company and test company come only after Rippling approves your partner application, which has no published timeline. Once in, a first sandbox OAuth install with Postman takes about an hour.

timeToProd.assumes: An App Shop partner app reading workers through public scopes, reaching the point where any company with your production listing URL can install (beta approval); public App Shop launch adds three external beta installs plus a Launch Review.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Partner application approval, then building required SSO and user-management capabilities, then Rippling's Integration Review (beta), plus approval for any private scopes.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Rippling publishes no review durations. The range is our estimate from the number of gated steps and required capabilities.

verdict.cost: No cost to partners for API use or App Shop listing, and no revenue share. Customers must have Rippling's Identity & Access Management package to install integrations.

prerequisites.item: Acceptance into the Rippling technology partner program
prerequisites.why: App listings, sandbox access and OAuth credentials are created only after your application is approved.

prerequisites.item: A product that can support SSO (SAML or OpenID Connect) and user management
prerequisites.why: Partner requirements describe Rippling-initiated and SP-initiated SSO and automatic user provisioning from Rippling employees; the Integration Review form checks SSO, user management and data sync.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Merge's guide says all integrations must support SAML SSO; Rippling's page lists SAML SSO and OIDC SSO sections.

prerequisites.item: Customers on Rippling's Identity & Access Management package
prerequisites.why: Required to install integrations built on Rippling's API, including beta installs.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Rippling's pricing page also says partners pay nothing to list and no revenue share is required.

prerequisites.item: Three external companies willing to beta test
prerequisites.why: Launch Review can only be submitted after at least three outside companies install the beta listing.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Needed only for public App Shop discovery, not for beta installs via your production URL.

scopeTiers.impact: Auto-approved when added to the listing. Every customer admin must consent to the full set; customers can't toggle individual scopes.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Scope strings taken from the example token response and SAML requirement; check the scope reference for current names.

scopeTiers.impact: Need a 'comprehensively documented business case' per scope. Rippling says access to private scopes is 'extremely limited'.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Which specific scopes are private isn't fully listed in what we could read; examples appear in the page FAQ.

scopeTiers.impact: New integrations should use the v2 REST API at https://rest.ripplingapis.com; access is the intersection of scopes and permissions. Call List companies after OAuth to bind the token to a company.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: workers.read appears in Rippling's llms.txt; whether each v2 scope is public or private wasn't confirmed.

steps.title: Apply to the technology partner program
steps.detail: Submit company details, customers and integration goals. If you use Merge, its CSM must apply for you.

steps.title: Wait for partner approval
steps.detail: Rippling decides at its discretion and may not explain rejections.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Discretionary approval is from Merge's guide; Rippling publishes no timeline.

steps.title: Create a draft app listing
steps.detail: In your partner company, create a listing: set display name, main category, icon, default redirect URL and scopes. Client ID and secret are under Integration > Credentials.

steps.title: Write private-scope business cases
steps.detail: For each private scope, draft why you need the data, what you'll do with it and the customer value.

steps.title: Build the Rippling-initiated install flow
steps.detail: Handle the redirect with code, buy and redirect_uri; have the user sign in to your app; exchange the code within 300 seconds at https://api.rippling.com/api/o/token/ with Basic auth; store tokens per company; call List companies and POST mark_app_installed; then redirect back to Rippling's return URL.

steps.title: Build SSO, user management and sync
steps.detail: Implement SAML or OIDC SSO with a 'Sign in with Rippling' button, employee.created/employee.deleted webhooks, automatic user matching and creation, and a manual sync button.

steps.title: Deploy and install the sandbox app
steps.detail: Deploy the sandbox listing, switch to your test company admin and run the install (Postman works well).

steps.title: Submit the Integration Review form
steps.detail: Includes requirement checklists, install flow videos, SSO, user management, data sync, support details, a test account and beta testers.

steps.title: Wait for beta approval
steps.detail: If approved, any company with your production listing URL (and the IAM package) can install. If rejected, fix and resubmit.

steps.title: Run beta with three companies and submit Launch Review
steps.detail: After three outside companies install, submit the Launch Review with integration documentation, then publish the listing.

blockers.symptom: No way to get OAuth credentials
blockers.cause: OAuth is only for approved App Shop partners; customer API tokens can't be used on behalf of another organization.
blockers.fix: Apply to the partner program, or use Rippling MCP for a user-identity connection.

blockers.symptom: Token exchange fails with an invalid or expired code
blockers.cause: Authorization codes expire after 300 seconds and are single-use.
blockers.fix: Exchange the code server-side immediately on redirect.

blockers.symptom: Rippling shows 'waiting for a connection request' after install
blockers.cause: No API call has been made yet for the new install.
blockers.fix: Call List companies and POST mark_app_installed right after the token exchange.

blockers.cause: The company doesn't have the Identity & Access Management package, or the installer isn't a Super Admin, Full Admin or App Admin.
blockers.fix: Have the customer add the IAM package and install as an eligible admin.

blockers.symptom: Fields come back null or 403 'Insufficient oauth scopes'
blockers.cause: Missing scope, or the data is redacted for the token.
blockers.fix: Add the scope (private ones need approval) and check __meta.redacted_fields.

blockers.symptom: Scope changes don't appear for an existing install
blockers.cause: Changes to a listing don't affect existing installs.
blockers.fix: Resync the sandbox app and reinstall or reauthorize.

nuances.text: Refresh tokens are single-use but have a 1-hour grace period after first use; access token lifetime comes from expires_in (129600 seconds, 36 hours, in Rippling's example).
One access token covers one Rippling company; twelve installing companies means twelve tokens.
Rate limits on rest.ripplingapis.com use a 10-second sliding window counted per token plus endpoint path (600 and 300 requests per 10 seconds are listed), with Retry-After on 429 and no lockout.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The page lists two limits; which applies to which traffic wasn't clear in what we could read.

nuances.text: Partners agree not to promise launch dates to customers or share the integration before Rippling approves beta testing.
Rippling's requirements say integrations built through third-party integration services aren't supported, yet Merge documents a CSM-led path; expect Rippling to decide case by case.
Page size can't exceed 100 and list endpoints must be paginated.
